h1: The 8 Best Printers for Small Spaces of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best printers for small spaces, from shelf-friendly Canon inkjets to a compact laser and a portable thermal model.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the best printer for small spaces, a compact quiet inkjet that fits a shelf or closet ledge. The TS6520 adds a small OLED display and automatic duplex, and the Brother HL-L2405W is a compact monochrome laser. The HP DeskJet 4355, Canon TR4720, TS3720 and MG3620 are inkjet alternatives, and the MT610Pro is an inkless thermal printer for a drawer.
intro: A printer for a small space is a different purchase from a printer for a house. The spec that decides it is where the machine will physically live and how loud it is when it wakes two feet from your bed. Features that make sense in a family home, like feeders and fax lines, turn into bulk you pay for with floor and shelf.

Eight printers went through a spec-sheet review here, and footprint, noise, wireless method and running cost set the order on the Primea score. Prices appear as buckets only. Footprints are described in words, not centimeters, because most listings skip dimensions, so measure the shelf you have in mind.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact, quiet inkjet that fits a shelf or closet ledge.
products.description:
The TS4320 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one that prints, copies and scans over standard home wifi. The listing describes it as friendly to shelf, desk or closet-ledge placement, with a quieter inkjet mechanism, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A quiet mechanism matters when the machine sits near a bed or a call area.

It ranks first because it balances footprint, noise and basic functions at a low price. The TS6520 adds a display and duplex, but at a similar footprint, so the cheaper TS4320 wins on simplicity.

Buy it for studio dwellers who need quiet and flexible placement. The caveats are a basic feature set and light-duty use. Skip it if you print large volumes.
products.idealFor: Studio apartment dwellers who need quiet and flexible placement.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen and auto duplex for printers that sit across the room.
products.description:
The TS6520 is a compact inkjet whose standout is a tiny 1.42 inch OLED screen, plus automatic two-sided printing. It also keeps the quiet inkjet mechanism. Wireless is the standard module, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A screen helps when the printer sits across the room, because you can read errors and settings without a phone.

It trails the TS4320 only because it is no smaller, and the extra features add little to a tiny space. Duplex saves paper and storage, which is a real small-space advantage.

Buy it for printers placed away from your desk. The caveats are that it is no smaller than the TS4320 and uses a standard wireless module. Skip it if you do not need duplex printing.
products.idealFor: Printers placed across the room from your desk.
products.skipIf: You do not need duplex printing.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A smaller footprint than any compact inkjet here, for documents only.
products.description:
This Brother is a print-only monochrome laser with a smaller footprint than the compact inkjet all-in-ones. It is Alexa compatible, and the toner does not dry out, in the $100 to $200 bucket. A laser's toner stays usable for months between jobs, which suits someone who prints once a week.

It ranks third because it prints but does not copy or scan, and it is louder when printing. For documents only, it is the smallest option with a conventional paper path.

Buy it for occasional document printers with a spare corner. The caveats are louder operation and no color. Skip it if you want to scan or print color.
products.idealFor: Occasional document printers with a spare corner.
products.skipIf: You want to scan or print color.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact HP all-in-one with a three-month Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one with a standard wifi module, HP Smart app setup and a three-month HP Instant Ink trial. It prints, scans and copies, in the $50 to $100 bucket. App-based setup makes it easy to join a network without cables.

It ranks behind the Canons because the listing makes no quiet claim and offers nothing on footprint beyond compact. The trial is a short-term bonus that does not change the hardware.

Buy it for easy app-based setup in a small apartment. The caveats are no quiet claim and standard wifi range. Skip it if noise is your top concern.
products.idealFor: Easy app-based setup in a small apartment.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Auto feeder and fax in a compact body that works on the floor.
products.description:
The TR4720 includes an auto document feeder and built-in fax in a compact all-in-one body, with wireless via the Canon PRINT app. The listing says it works for floor or corner placement, in the $50 to $100 bucket. A feeder helps with stacks of paper, but it adds bulk to the body.

It ranks fifth because the feeder and fax add size that small spaces rarely need. Floor placement is a useful flexibility, however, for apartments without a shelf.

Buy it for small home offices with paperwork and little shelf space. The caveats are the extra bulk and a fax line few use. Skip it if you never scan multi-page documents.
products.idealFor: Small home offices with paperwork and little shelf space.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: The smallest full all-in-one here, with no duplex.
products.description:
The TS3720 is a basic compact color all-in-one with the smallest footprint among the full all-in-one picks, a quiet inkjet mechanism and wireless via the Canon PRINT app. It has no auto duplex, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Minimal hardware means less to occupy a shelf.

It sits below the TS4320 because it has fewer features for similar money, though it saves a little space. Without duplex, double-sided printing is manual.

Buy it for tight budgets in noise-sensitive rooms. The caveats are no auto duplex and a basic feature set. Skip it if you want two-sided printing.

products.name: Canon Pixma MG3620 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact inkjet with solid photo output and mobile printing.
products.description:
The MG3620 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one with mobile and tablet printing, a quiet inkjet mechanism, a standard wifi module and solid photo print quality per the listing. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket. Photo-capable inkjets suit someone who prints the occasional picture.

It ranks lower because the higher price bracket buys an older design with no clear edge in size. It beats the thermal printer on paper compatibility.

Buy it for occasional photo printing alongside documents. The caveats are the higher bracket and its age. Skip it if you only print text.

products.name: Inkless Portable Bluetooth Thermal Printer (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: Stores in a drawer, but needs its own thermal paper.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is an inkless thermal printer at 300 DPI that supports Letter and A4 paper. It connects over Bluetooth, which sidesteps router range, and it stores in a drawer between uses, in the $50 to $100 bucket. No ink means no cartridges drying out in a closet.

It ranks last because it prints only on proprietary thermal paper, and quality for daily use is limited. It is the right answer only when floor and shelf are both gone.

Buy it for the most space-constrained studios. The caveats are the proprietary paper and limited daily quality. Skip it if you print daily and want standard paper.
products.skipIf: You print daily and want standard paper.

whatMatters.detail: Shelf, desk, corner and drawer are different jobs. A shelf printer needs a small body, while a drawer printer needs to be portable. Check the listing's placement language before choosing, and measure the actual spot, because a printer that needs rear clearance for paper trays will not fit flush against a wall. Leave room for the output tray to open.

Inkjets are quieter than lasers when printing. This matters in a studio where the printer sits near your bed or call area. Look for the words quiet mechanism in the bullets, as on the Canon PIXMA models, and remember that the Brother laser is louder during active printing. Noise matters most for a printer within arm's reach of a bed.

A standard wifi module needs router range, while Bluetooth does not. Check this if the printer will sit far from your router. A printer in a closet behind two walls can drop its connection, and a Bluetooth device avoids the problem at the cost of simpler functions. A wifi extender can help, but adds another box.

A document feeder and fax add bulk. If you never scan stacks of paper, skip them. Read the title for feeder or fax mentions, and favor a basic all-in-one if your printing is mostly single pages, because extra hardware takes space you cannot spare. Count the sheets you scan in a month before you decide.

Inkjets can dry out, toner does not, and thermal needs special paper. Pick the type that fits how often you print. A weekly printer suits laser toner, while a daily printer suits an inkjet, and the thermal option makes sense only if you accept proprietary paper. Replacement cost adds up over a year.

howToChoose.intro: Where the printer lives decides the model.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Quieter and does color. The Canon TS models, MG3620 and HP DeskJet 4355.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Smaller than compact inkjets and the toner does not dry out. The Brother HL-L2405W.

howToChoose.note: Most small-space buyers should default to an inkjet unless they print only black documents.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A quiet mechanism and a shelf-friendly body.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 lists both and is the pick here.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want duplex and a display, which the TS6520 adds, or photo quality from the MG3620.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Light use. The TS3720 covers basics with the smallest all-in-one body.

faq.a: The Canon PIXMA TS models and the MG3620 list a quiet inkjet mechanism. The Brother laser is louder when printing, and the HP DeskJet makes no quiet claim. Pick a Canon inkjet if the printer sleeps near you.

faq.q: What mistake do small-space buyers make?
faq.a: Buying a feature-heavy model, then losing shelf space to a feeder they never use. The TS4320 shows that basic can be enough, and a smaller body leaves more room for what you actually use.

faq.q: Is a laser worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: A laser's toner does not dry out and its footprint is smaller, but it prints black only here. The Brother HL-L2405W suits occasional documents, and its toner will not dry out between jobs. It does not copy or scan, however.

faq.q: How do I set up the Canon models?
faq.a: Use the Canon PRINT app over wifi. The HP DeskJet 4355 uses the HP Smart app, and setup is quick on both. Keep the printer on the same network as your phone during setup.

faq.q: Does the thermal printer need ink?
faq.a: No, but it requires proprietary thermal paper, which you must reorder from the maker. The MT610Pro stores in a drawer, which suits the tightest spaces. Check the cost of its paper before buying.

faq.q: Can I keep the printer far from my router?
faq.a: Standard wifi models need range. The MT610Pro uses Bluetooth, which avoids that, though other printers can use an extender. Moving the router closer is the free fix, and a repeater costs little if that fails.

finalTake: Buy the TS4320 for a studio where space and noise both matter, and the TS6520 if the printer sits across the room. The Brother laser suits occasional black documents, and the TS3720 is the smallest full all-in-one. The MT610Pro is for the most cramped homes, but it needs its own paper. Measure the spot before you order, because footprint beats features here.
